message_preview: Fake CS2 skin gambling site csgotune.com (Oct 2026). The site showed a large fake withdrawable balance, then demanded ID documents and repeated 'verification / unlock' crypto deposits (ETH and USDT on Ethereum) to release a withdrawal that never arrived. The site's 'support' contacts (the site's support mailbox, Gmail accounts and Telegram accounts @alexrodeo, @ultratronx, @prettymoonx and others) then switched to extortion: they demanded 2 ETH, later 1.5 ETH, threatening to sell or publish the victim's ID documents, doxxed the victim on subdomains of csgotune.com and threatened his family. They also ran a fake Steam login page and a fake 'KYC deletion' page (deletekyc.csgotune.com) that harvests emails and passwords. On 31 Oct 2026 they impersonated Hostinger's abuse team from a Gmail account to ask for the victim's phone number. The victim paid 12 transfers, about USD 9,900, mostly to 0x09e5Ee44B14857e53B1412D41DDc3DDB504F36c8, which forwarded funds to exchange deposit addresses at Bybit (0xF1B0785DAd2A73D170EE3f863B38F7004b03Bc9A) and WhiteBIT (0x2b088a07EA261eC724B0c9F7996bc093fE7D25D2). The sender threatened to distribute the alleged material to my personal and professional contacts unless I paid $1,500 in Bitcoin within 24 hours.
full_message:
I received an extortion email from an unknown individual claiming to have hacked my computer and stolen personal information, photos, and private recordings. The sender threatened to distribute the alleged material to my personal and professional contacts unless I paid $1,500 in Bitcoin within 24 hours.

The email included a Bitcoin wallet address and attempted to pressure me into making an immediate payment by claiming that a countdown had started. The sender also listed multiple login credentials associated with online services. However, these credentials appear to be outdated, and the passwords had already been changed long ago.

I have not made any payment and do not intend to comply with the threat. I am reporting the Bitcoin wallet address because it was provided as the destination for the demanded extortion payment. I am concerned that this wallet may be used to receive funds obtained through threats, blackmail, or other fraudulent activity.

I request that this wallet address and the associated activity be reviewed for potential links to extortion or other financial crimes. I can provide the original email and its headers as supporting evidence if needed.
